alignments.note: Complementizer realized by that; the clause is reported speech with the word written, so rule 43's unrepresented case does not apply.
Anarthrous noun with the supplied indefinite as its rule 7 helper under rule 51's anarthrous clause.
Attributive adjective rendered sacred; SBLGNT.2TI.3.15.v005 is underdetermined and the projection's base reading stands.
Both adjective and noun are anarthrous in the projection, so under rule 58 the supplied the belongs to the noun, discontinuously under rule 15.
Perfect indicative with its supplied subject and auxiliary, headed on the lexical verb.
Second attributive article governing an expressed head noun with a participle following; rule 31 makes it unrepresented and gives the relativizer to the participle.
Attributive participle rendered as a finite relative clause; the relativizer and copula are its rule 31 helpers, headed on able.
Infinitive rendered by the resultative make wise, discontinuous around thee; rule 17 heads such a rendering on the meaning-bearing complement, as make straight heads on straight.
Noun rendered faith, with no determiner written.
Article following its noun with a prepositional phrase as its modifier; rule 31 gives it the supplied relativizer, no determiner having been written for the noun.
A prepositional phrase has no verb to carry the supplied copula, so under rules 31 and 53 the preposition takes it, headed on the prepositional word.
Name, split from Jesus under rule 26.

review_notes: The two attributive articles are treated differently by rule 31's own test: ta governs a participle and is unrepresented, while tēs governs a prepositional phrase and keeps the relativizer.
The supplied the of the sacred writings goes to the anarthrous noun under rule 58, the following article having been emptied by rule 31.
